The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# gotests

**gotests** is a powerful Go test generator that automatically creates table-driven tests from your source code. It analyzes function and method signatures to generate comprehensive test scaffolding, saving you time and ensuring consistency across your test suite.

## Key Features

- 🚀 **Zero-config test generation** - Works out of the box with any Go project
- 🎯 **Smart test scaffolding** - Generates complete table-driven test structure with proper type handling
- 🔧 **Flexible filtering** - Generate tests for specific functions, exported functions, or entire packages
- 📦 **Auto-imports** - Automatically adds required imports to test files
- 🧬 **Full generics support** - Works seamlessly with Go 1.18+ type parameters
- 🔄 **Recursive generation** - Process entire directory trees with `./...` pattern
- 🎨 **Custom templates** - Built-in support for testify and custom test templates
- ⚡ **Parallel subtests** - Optional parallel test execution support

## Installation

**Minimum Go version:** Go 1.22

Use `go install` to install and update:

```sh
$ go install github.com/cweill/gotests/gotests@latest
```

## Usage

From the commandline, `gotests` can generate Go tests for specific source files or an entire directory. By default, it prints its output to `stdout`.

```sh
$ gotests [options] PATH ...
```

### Available Options

```
  -all                  generate tests for all functions and methods

  -excl                 regexp. generate tests for functions and methods that don't
                         match. Takes precedence over -only, -exported, and -all

  -exported             generate tests for exported functions and methods. Takes
                         precedence over -only and -all

  -i                    print test inputs in error messages

  -named                switch table tests from using slice to map (with test name for the key)

  -only                 regexp. generate tests for functions and methods that match only.
                         Takes precedence over -all

  -nosubtests           disable subtest generation when >= Go 1.7

  -parallel             enable parallel subtest generation when >= Go 1.7.

  -w                    write output to (test) files instead of stdout

  -template_dir         Path to a directory containing custom test code templates. Takes
                         precedence over -template. This can also be set via environment
                         variable GOTESTS_TEMPLATE_DIR

  -template             Specify custom test code templates, e.g. testify. This can also
                         be set via environment variable GOTESTS_TEMPLATE

  -template_params_file read external parameters to template by json with file

  -template_params      read external parameters to template by json with stdin

  -use_go_cmp           use cmp.Equal (google/go-cmp) instead of reflect.DeepEqual

  -ai                   generate test cases using AI (requires Ollama)

  -ai-model             AI model to use (default "qwen2.5-coder:0.5b")

  -ai-endpoint          Ollama API endpoint (default "http://localhost:11434")

  -ai-min-cases         minimum number of test cases to generate with AI (default 3)

  -ai-max-cases         maximum number of test cases to generate with AI (default 10)

  -version              print version information and exit
```

## Quick Start Examples

### Generate tests for a single function

Given a file `math.go`:

```go
package math

func Add(a, b int) int {
    return a + b
}
```

Generate a test:

```sh
$ gotests -only Add -w math.go
```

This creates `math_test.go` with:

```go
func TestAdd(t *testing.T) {
    type args struct {
        a int
        b int
    }
    tests := []struct {
        name string
        args args
        want int
    }{
        // TODO: Add test cases.
    }
    for _, tt := range tests {
        t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            if got := Add(tt.args.a, tt.args.b); got != tt.want {
                t.Errorf("Add() = %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
            }
        })
    }
}
```

### Generate tests for all exported functions

```sh
$ gotests -all -exported -w .
```

This generates tests for all exported functions in the current directory.

### Generate tests recursively

```sh
$ gotests -all -w ./...
```

This generates tests for all functions in the current directory and all subdirectories.

### Generate tests with testify

```sh
$ gotests -all -template testify -w calculator.go
```

This generates tests using the testify assertion library.

### Common workflows

```sh
# Generate tests for all exported functions in a package
$ gotests -exported -w pkg/*.go

### Usage

```sh
# Generate tests with AI-powered test cases (uses default model)
$ gotests -all -ai -w calculator.go

# Use a different model

# Use custom Ollama endpoint

```

### How It Works

When you use the `-ai` flag, `gotests`:
1. Generates the standard table-driven test structure
2. Sends the function signature and body to the local LLM
3. The LLM analyzes the code and generates realistic test cases
4. Populates the test table with these cases instead of `// TODO: Add test cases.`

### Supported Features

✅ Functions with multiple parameters
✅ Functions with multiple return values
✅ Error handling test cases
✅ Edge cases and boundary conditions
✅ Methods with receivers

### Privacy & Security

**What data is sent to the LLM:**
- Function signatures (name, parameters, return types)
- Complete function bodies including all code and comments
- No file paths or project context

**Privacy considerations:**
- ⚠️ **Function bodies may contain sensitive information** - business logic, algorithms, or credentials/secrets in comments
- ✅ **Local-first by default** - Using Ollama keeps all data on your machine; nothing is sent to external servers
- ✅ **Offline operation** - AI generation works completely offline with local models
- 🔒 **Recommendation**: Avoid using `-ai` on code containing secrets, API keys, or proprietary algorithms in comments

**If using cloud providers in the future:**
- Function source code will be transmitted to the cloud provider's API
- Review the provider's data retention and privacy policies
- Consider using `-ai` only on non-sensitive codebases

## Go Generics Support

`gotests` fully supports Go generics (type parameters) introduced in Go 1.18+. It automatically generates tests for generic functions and methods on generic types.

### Example: Generic Function

Given this generic function:

```go
func FindFirst[T comparable](slice []T, target T) (int, error) {
    for i, v := range slice {
        if v == target {
            return i, nil
        }
    }
    return -1, ErrNotFound
}
```

Running `gotests -all -w yourfile.go` generates:

```go
func TestFindFirst(t *testing.T) {
    type args struct {
        slice  []string
        target string
    }
    tests := []struct {
        name    string
        args    args
        want    int
        wantErr bool
    }{
        // TODO: Add test cases.
    }
    for _, tt := range tests {
        t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            got, err := FindFirst[string](tt.args.slice, tt.args.target)
            if (err != nil) != tt.wantErr {
                t.Errorf("FindFirst() error = %v, wantErr %v", err, tt.wantErr)
                return
            }
            if got != tt.want {
                t.Errorf("FindFirst() = %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
            }
        })
    }
}
```

### Example: Methods on Generic Types

`gotests` also supports methods on generic types:

```go
type Set[T comparable] struct {
    m map[T]struct{}
}

func (s *Set[T]) Add(v T) {
    if s.m == nil {
        s.m = make(map[T]struct{})
    }
    s.m[v] = struct{}{}
}
```

Generates:

```go
func TestSet_Add(t *testing.T) {
    type args struct {
        v string
    }
    tests := []struct {
        name string
        s    *Set[string]
        args args
    }{
        // TODO: Add test cases.
    }
    for _, tt := range tests {
        t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            s := &Set[string]{}
            s.Add(tt.args.v)
        })
    }
}
```

### Type Constraint Mapping

`gotests` uses intelligent defaults for type parameter instantiation:

- `any` → `int`
- `comparable` → `string`
- Union types (`int64 | float64`) → first option (`int64`)
- Approximation constraints (`~int`) → underlying type (`int`)

This ensures generated tests use appropriate concrete types for testing generic code.

## Editor Plugins

`gotests` integrates with many popular editors:

- [Visual Studio Code](https://github.com/golang/vscode-go/blob/master/docs/settings.md#gogeneratetestsflags) (built-in to Go extension)
- [Sublime Text](https://github.com/cweill/GoTests-Sublime)

# gotests

**gotests** is a powerful Go test generator that automatically creates table-driven tests from your source code. It analyzes function and method signatures to generate comprehensive test scaffolding, saving you time and ensuring consistency across your test suite.

## Key Features

- 🚀 **Zero-config test generation** - Works out of the box with any Go project
- 🎯 **Smart test scaffolding** - Generates complete table-driven test structure with proper type handling
- 🔧 **Flexible filtering** - Generate tests for specific functions, exported functions, or entire packages
- 📦 **Auto-imports** - Automatically adds required imports to test files
- 🧬 **Full generics support** - Works seamlessly with Go 1.18+ type parameters
- 🔄 **Recursive generation** - Process entire directory trees with `./...` pattern
- 🎨 **Custom templates** - Built-in support for testify and custom test templates
- ⚡ **Parallel subtests** - Optional parallel test execution support

## Installation

**Minimum Go version:** Go 1.22

Use `go install` to install and update:

```sh
$ go install github.com/cweill/gotests/gotests@latest
```

## Usage

From the commandline, `gotests` can generate Go tests for specific source files or an entire directory. By default, it prints its output to `stdout`.

```sh
$ gotests [options] PATH ...
```

### Available Options

```
  -all                  generate tests for all functions and methods

  -excl                 regexp. generate tests for functions and methods that don't
                         match. Takes precedence over -only, -exported, and -all

  -exported             generate tests for exported functions and methods. Takes
                         precedence over -only and -all

  -i                    print test inputs in error messages

  -named                switch table tests from using slice to map (with test name for the key)

  -only                 regexp. generate tests for functions and methods that match only.
                         Takes precedence over -all

  -nosubtests           disable subtest generation when >= Go 1.7

  -parallel             enable parallel subtest generation when >= Go 1.7.

  -w                    write output to (test) files instead of stdout

  -template_dir         Path to a directory containing custom test code templates. Takes
                         precedence over -template. This can also be set via environment
                         variable GOTESTS_TEMPLATE_DIR

  -template             Specify custom test code templates, e.g. testify. This can also
                         be set via environment variable GOTESTS_TEMPLATE

  -template_params_file read external parameters to template by json with file

  -template_params      read external parameters to template by json with stdin

  -use_go_cmp           use cmp.Equal (google/go-cmp) instead of reflect.DeepEqual

  -ai                   generate test cases using AI (requires Ollama)

  -ai-model             AI model to use (default "qwen2.5-coder:0.5b")

  -ai-endpoint          Ollama API endpoint (default "http://localhost:11434")

  -ai-min-cases         minimum number of test cases to generate with AI (default 3)

  -ai-max-cases         maximum number of test cases to generate with AI (default 10)

  -version              print version information and exit
```

## Quick Start Examples

### Generate tests for a single function

Given a file `math.go`:

```go
package math

func Add(a, b int) int {
    return a + b
}
```

Generate a test:

```sh
$ gotests -only Add -w math.go
```

This creates `math_test.go` with:

```go
func TestAdd(t *testing.T) {
    type args struct {
        a int
        b int
    }
    tests := []struct {
        name string
        args args
        want int
    }{
        // TODO: Add test cases.
    }
    for _, tt := range tests {
        t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            if got := Add(tt.args.a, tt.args.b); got != tt.want {
                t.Errorf("Add() = %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
            }
        })
    }
}
```

### Generate tests for all exported functions

```sh
$ gotests -all -exported -w .
```

This generates tests for all exported functions in the current directory.

### Generate tests recursively

```sh
$ gotests -all -w ./...
```

This generates tests for all functions in the current directory and all subdirectories.

### Generate tests with testify

```sh
$ gotests -all -template testify -w calculator.go
```

This generates tests using the testify assertion library.

### Common workflows

```sh
# Generate tests for all exported functions in a package
$ gotests -exported -w pkg/*.go

# Generate only tests for specific functions matching a pattern
$ gotests -only "^Process" -w handler.go

# Generate tests excluding certain functions
$ gotests -all -excl "^helper" -w utils.go

# Generate parallel subtests
$ gotests -all -parallel -w service.go
```

## AI-Powered Test Generation

**gotests** can generate intelligent test cases

### How It Works

When you use the `-ai` flag, `gotests`:
1. Generates the standard table-driven test structure
2. Sends the function signature and body to the local LLM
3. The LLM analyzes the code and generates realistic test cases
4. Populates the test table with these cases instead of `// TODO: Add test cases.`

### Supported Features

✅ Functions with multiple parameters
✅ Functions with multiple return values
✅ Error handling test cases
✅ Edge cases and boundary conditions
✅ Methods with receivers

### Privacy & Security

**What data is sent to the LLM:**
- Function signatures (name, parameters, return types)
- Complete function bodies including all code and comments
- No file paths or project context

**Privacy considerations:**
- ⚠️ **Function bodies may contain sensitive information** - business logic, algorithms, or credentials/secrets in comments
- ✅ **Local-first by default** - Using Ollama keeps all data on your machine; nothing is sent to external servers
- ✅ **Offline operation** - AI generation works completely offline with local models
- 🔒 **Recommendation**: Avoid using `-ai` on code containing secrets, API keys, or proprietary algorithms in comments

**If using cloud providers in the future:**
- Function source code will be transmitted to the cloud provider's API
- Review the provider's data retention and privacy policies
- Consider using `-ai` only on non-sensitive codebases

## Go Generics Support

`gotests` fully supports Go generics (type parameters) introduced in Go 1.18+. It automatically generates tests for generic functions and methods on generic types.

### Example: Generic Function

Given this generic function:

```go
func FindFirst[T comparable](slice []T, target T) (int, error) {
    for i, v := range slice {
        if v == target {
            return i, nil
        }
    }
    return -1, ErrNotFound
}
```

Running `gotests -all -w yourfile.go` generates:

```go
func TestFindFirst(t *testing.T) {
    type args struct {
        slice  []string
        target string
    }
    tests := []struct {
        name    string
        args    args
        want    int
        wantErr bool
    }{
        // TODO: Add test cases.
    }
    for _, tt := range tests {
        t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            got, err := FindFirst[string](tt.args.slice, tt.args.target)
            if (err != nil) != tt.wantErr {
                t.Errorf("FindFirst() error = %v, wantErr %v", err, tt.wantErr)
                return
            }
            if got != tt.want {
                t.Errorf("FindFirst() = %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
            }
        })
    }
}
```

### Example: Methods on Generic Types

`gotests` also supports methods on generic types:

```go
type Set[T comparable] struct {
    m map[T]struct{}
}

func (s *Set[T]) Add(v T) {
    if s.m == nil {
        s.m = make(map[T]struct{})
    }
    s.m[v] = struct{}{}
}
```

Generates:

```go
func TestSet_Add(t *testing.T) {
    type args struct {
        v string
    }
    tests := []struct {
        name string
        s    *Set[string]
        args args
    }{
        // TODO: Add test cases.
    }
    for _, tt := range tests {
        t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            s := &Set[string]{}
            s.Add(tt.args.v)
        })
    }
}
```

### Type Constraint Mapping

`gotests` uses intelligent defaults for type parameter instantiation:

- `any` → `int`
- `comparable` → `string`
- Union types (`int64 | float64`) → first option (`int64`)
- Approximation constraints (`~int`) → underlying type (`int`)

This ensures generated tests use appropriate concrete types for testing generic code.

## Editor Plugins

`gotests` integrates with many popular editors:

- [Visual Studio Code](https://github.com/golang/vscode-go/blob/master/docs/settings.md#gogeneratetestsflags) (built-in to Go extension)
- [Sublime Text](https://github.com/cweill/GoTests-Sublime)
- [Vim](https://github.com/buoto/gotests-vim)
- [Emacs](https://github.com/damienlevin/GoTests-Emacs) or [alternative](https://github.com/s-kostyaev/go-gen-test)
- [Atom](https://atom.io/packages/gotests)
- [IntelliJ GoLand](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/go/run-debug-configuration-for-go-test.html)

func concreteForConstraint(expr ast.Expr) string {
	switch t := expr.(type) {
	case *ast.Ident:
		if t.Name == "any" {
			return "int"
		}
		if t.Name == "comparable" {
			return "string"
		}
		if t.Name == "Ordered" {
			return "int"
		}
		return "string"
	case *ast.SelectorExpr:
		if t.Sel != nil && t.Sel.Name == "Ordered" {
			return "int"
		}
		return "string"
	case *ast.UnaryExpr:
		return exprToString(t.X, nil)
	case *ast.BinaryExpr:
		left := t.X
		for {
			if b, ok := left.(*ast.BinaryExpr); ok {
				left = b.X
				continue
			}
			break
		}
		if u, ok := left.(*ast.UnaryExpr); ok {
			return exprToString(u.X, nil)
		}
		return exprToString(left, nil)
	case *ast.InterfaceType:
		if t.Methods != nil {
			for _, f := range t.Methods.List {
				if b, ok := f.Type.(*ast.BinaryExpr); ok {
					left := b.X
					for {
						if bb, ok := left.(*ast.BinaryExpr); ok {
							left = bb.X
							continue
						}
						break
					}
					if u, ok := left.(*ast.UnaryExpr); ok {
						return exprToString(u.X, nil)
					}
					return exprToString(left, nil)
				}
				if u, ok := f.Type.(*ast.UnaryExpr); ok {
					return exprToString(u.X, nil)
				}
			}
		}
		return "string"
	default:
		return "string"
	}
}

func exprToString(expr ast.Expr, typeMap map[string]string) string {
	if expr == nil {
		return ""
	}
	switch t := expr.(type) {
	case *ast.Ident:
		if typeMap != nil {
			if v, ok := typeMap[t.Name]; ok {
				return v
			}
		}
		return t.Name
	case *ast.SelectorExpr:
		return exprToString(t.X, typeMap) + "." + t.Sel.Name
	case *ast.StarExpr:
		return "*" + exprToString(t.X, typeMap)
	case *ast.ArrayType:
		if t.Len == nil {
			return "[]" + exprToString(t.Elt, typeMap)
		}
		return "[" + exprToString(t.Len, typeMap) + "]" + exprToString(t.Elt, typeMap)
	case *ast.MapType:
		return "map[" + exprToString(t.Key, typeMap) + "]" + exprToString(t.Value, typeMap)
	case *ast.ChanType:
		switch t.Dir {
		case ast.SEND:
			return "chan<- " + exprToString(t.Value, typeMap)
		case ast.RECV:
			return "<-chan " + exprToString(t.Value, typeMap)
		default:
			return "chan " + exprToString(t.Value, typeMap)
		}
	case *ast.FuncType:
		return funcTypeToString(t, typeMap)
	case *ast.InterfaceType:
		if t.Methods == nil || len(t.Methods.List) == 0 {
			return "interface{}"
		}
		return "interface{}"
	case *ast.StructType:
		if t.Fields == nil || len(t.Fields.List) == 0 {
			return "struct{}"
		}
		var parts []string
		for _, f := range t.Fields.List {
			typeStr := exprToString(f.Type, typeMap)
			if len(f.Names) == 0 {
				parts = append(parts, typeStr)
			} else {
				for _, n := range f.Names {
					parts = append(parts, n.Name+" "+typeStr)
				}
			}
		}
		return "struct{ " + strings.Join(parts, "; ") + " }"
	case *ast.Ellipsis:
		return "[]" + exprToString(t.Elt, typeMap)
	case *ast.BasicLit:
		return t.Value
	case *ast.ParenExpr:
		return exprToString(t.X, typeMap)
	case *ast.IndexExpr:
		return exprToString(t.X, typeMap) + "[" + exprToString(t.Index, typeMap) + "]"
	case *ast.IndexListExpr:
		var parts []string
		for _, e := range t.Indices {
			parts = append(parts, exprToString(e, typeMap))
		}
		return exprToString(t.X, typeMap) + "[" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + "]"
	default:
		return "interface{}"
	}
}

func funcTypeToString(ft *ast.FuncType, typeMap map[string]string) string {
	var params []string
	if ft.Params != nil {
		for _, f := range ft.Params.List {
			typeStr := exprToString(f.Type, typeMap)
			if len(f.Names) == 0 {
				params = append(params, typeStr)
			} else {
				for _, n := range f.Names {
					params = append(params, n.Name+" "+typeStr)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	s := "func(" + strings.Join(params, ", ") + ")"
	if ft.Results != nil && len(ft.Results.List) > 0 {
		if len(ft.Results.List) == 1 && len(ft.Results.List[0].Names) == 0 {
			s += " " + exprToString(ft.Results.List[0].Type, typeMap)
		} else {
			var res []string
			for _, f := range ft.Results.List {
				typeStr := exprToString(f.Type, typeMap)
				if len(f.Names) == 0 {
					res = append(res, typeStr)
				} else {
					for _, n := range f.Names {
						res = append(res, n.Name+" "+typeStr)
					}
				}
			}
			s += " (" + strings.Join(res, ", ") + ")"
		}
	}
	return s
}

func isErrorType(expr ast.Expr) bool {
	id, ok := expr.(*ast.Ident)
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	return id.Name == "error"
}

func isBasicComparable(name string) bool {
	switch name {
	case "bool", "string",
		"int", "int8", "int16", "int32", "int64",
		"uint", "uint8", "uint16", "uint32", "uint64", "uintptr",
		"float32", "float64", "complex64", "complex128",
		"byte", "rune":
		return true
	}
	return false
}

func needsDeepEqualForType(expr ast.Expr, typeMap map[string]string) bool {
	// Determine if type needs reflect.DeepEqual (true) vs == (false)
	// typeMap is for generics substitution? Actually decision for generic T based on constraint, not inst?
	// For now, handle non-generic; for generic T (Ident in typeMap keys), decide based on constraint? Caller should handle generic separately.
	switch t := expr.(type) {

		// Check if it's a type param (in typeMap)? If so, need to decide based on constraint? But typeMap maps T->concrete, not constraint.
		// For generic, we need separate logic. For now, if Ident is in typeMap (i.e., is type param), return true (DeepEqual) unless constraint is basic?
		// Caller will handle generic case separately, so here assume non-generic.
		if t.Name == "any" || t.Name == "interface" {
			return true
		}
		if isBasicComparable(t.Name) {
			return false
		}
		// For other idents (like S, MyStruct, time? No, time is selector), e.g., S struct? Struct types as Ident (named struct) -> DeepEqual
		// For named types like MyInt (int underlying) - should it be == or DeepEqual? Earlier MyInt? Not tested. For S struct, DeepEqual.
		// For safety, return true for non-basic idents (like S, MyStruct, etc.)
		return true
	case *ast.StarExpr:
		// *T: check element
		// Unwrap?
		elt := t.X
		// If elt is Ident basic -> false, else true?
		// For *int -> false, *error (error is Ident "error"? error is interface, not basic) -> true, *MyErr (struct) -> true
		if id, ok := elt.(*ast.Ident); ok {
			if isBasicComparable(id.Name) {
				return false
			}
			return true
		}
		// For *struct, *slice, etc. -> true
		return true
	case *ast.SelectorExpr:

	case *ast.ArrayType, *ast.MapType, *ast.StructType, *ast.ChanType, *ast.FuncType, *ast.InterfaceType, *ast.MapType:
		return true
	default:

	}
}

func processSingleFile(srcPath, displayPath string, allFlag, exportedFlag bool, onlyStr, exclStr string, onlyRe, exclRe *regexp.Regexp, iFlag, namedFlag, nosubtestsFlag, parallelFlag, useGoCmpFlag, wFlag, aiFlag bool, aiEndpoint, aiModel string, aiMin, aiMax int, tmplDir, tmplName string, useCustomDir bool, suppressNoTests bool) {
	printed := processSingleFileCollect(srcPath, displayPath, allFlag, exportedFlag, onlyStr, exclStr, onlyRe, exclRe, iFlag, namedFlag, nosubtestsFlag, parallelFlag, useGoCmpFlag, wFlag, aiFlag, aiEndpoint, aiModel, aiMin, aiMax, tmplDir, tmplName, useCustomDir)
	if !printed && !suppressNoTests {
		fmt.Printf("No tests generated for %s\n", displayPath)
	}

func processSingleFileCollect(srcPath, displayPath string, allFlag, exportedFlag bool, onlyStr, exclStr string, onlyRe, exclRe *regexp.Regexp, iFlag, namedFlag, nosubtestsFlag, parallelFlag, useGoCmpFlag, wFlag, aiFlag bool, aiEndpoint, aiModel string, aiMin, aiMax int, tmplDir, tmplName string, useCustomDir bool) bool {
	fset := token.NewFileSet()
	srcFile, err := parser.ParseFile(fset, srcPath, nil, parser.ParseComments)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("Parser.Parse source file: target parser.ParseFile(): %v\n", err)
		return true
	}
	dir := filepath.Dir(srcPath)
	otherFiles, otherErrPath, otherErr := parseOtherFiles(dir, srcPath, fset)
	if otherErr != nil {
		_ = otherErrPath
		fmt.Printf("Parser.Parse source file: other file parser.ParseFile: %v\n", otherErr)

	_ = otherFiles
	_ = srcFile
	// Check if src is _test.go and handle skipping Test* later

	// For srcPath like /tmp/foo.go, testPath is /tmp/foo_test.go (same dir, base without .go + _test.go)

	// When input is foo_test.go with Helper+TestFoo, output preserved Helper+TestFoo (from src) + new TestHelper. So it treats src as both source and existing? Or it reads src as source (to find Helper to generate) and also as existing (to preserve)?
	// For source file foo.go with foo_test.go existing, output preserves foo_test.go content + new.
	// So logic: if src is test file, existing content is src itself; if src is source, existing content is corresponding _test.go if exists.
	testPath := ""
	if isTestFile {
		testPath = srcPath
	} else {
		ext := filepath.Ext(srcPath)
		base := strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(srcPath), ext)
		testPath = filepath.Join(dir, base+"_test.go")
	}
	// Parse test file if exists (and if not same as src? For test file src, we already have srcFile parsed; but need to parse again for existing funcs? Use srcFile as test file? But srcFile is already parsed as source. For test file src, source and test are same file. Need to handle separately.)
	var testFile *ast.File

		if testPath == srcPath {

			}
			testFile = tf
			testFileExists = true
		}
	}
	_ = testFileExists

	return true
}

func parseOtherFiles(dir, srcPath string, fset *token.FileSet) (map[string]*ast.File, string, error) {
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", nil
	}
	m := make(map[string]*ast.File)
	for _, e := range entries {
		if e.IsDir() {
			continue
		}
		name := e.Name()
		if !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".go") {
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasSuffix(name, "_test.go") {
			continue
		}
		full := filepath.Join(dir, name)
		if full == srcPath {
			continue
		}
		// Need to handle relative vs absolute: srcPath as given might be "a.go" while full is "a.go"? For dir "." with src "a.go", full "a.go" matches? filepath.Join(".", "a.go") = "a.go". Good. For absolute, matches.
		// But what if srcPath is "./a.go" vs "a.go"? They are same file but strings differ. Use cleaned comparison?
		if filepath.Clean(full) == filepath.Clean(srcPath) {
			continue
		}
		f, err := parser.ParseFile(fset, full, nil, parser.ParseComments)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, full, err
		}
		m[full] = f
	}
	return m, "", nil
}

		name := fd.Name.Name
		// Skip Test* in test files
		if isTestFile && strings.HasPrefix(name, "Test") {
			continue
		}
		isMethod := fd.Recv != nil && len(fd.Recv.List) > 0
		var recvName string
		var recvTypeAST ast.Expr
		var recvTypeBase string
		var recvIsPtr bool
		if isMethod {
			rf := fd.Recv.List[0]
			if len(rf.Names) > 0 {
				recvName = rf.Names[0].Name
			}
			recvTypeAST = rf.Type
			recvTypeBase, recvIsPtr = baseTypeName(rf.Type)
		}
		// Filtering
		if exportedOnly {
			if !isExported(name) {
				continue
			}
		}
		if onlyRe != nil {
			if !matchesWithTitle(onlyRe, recvTypeBase, name, isMethod) {
				continue
			}
		}
		if exclRe != nil {
			if matchesWithTitle(exclRe, recvTypeBase, name, isMethod) {
				continue
			}
		}
		// Build FuncInfo (params, results, etc. will be filled later)
		fi := FuncInfo{
			Name: name,
			IsMethod: isMethod,
			RecvName: recvName,
			RecvType: recvTypeBase,
			RecvTypeAST: recvTypeAST,
			RecvIsPointer: recvIsPtr,
			Decl: fd,
		}
		if isMethod {
			fi.TestName = testNameForMethod(recvTypeBase, name)
		} else {
			fi.TestName = testNameForFunc(name)
		}
		out = append(out, fi)
	}
	return out
}

func baseTypeName(expr ast.Expr) (string, bool) {
	// Returns base type name and isPointer
	switch t := expr.(type) {
	case *ast.Ident:
		return t.Name, false
	case *ast.StarExpr:
		base, _ := baseTypeName(t.X)
		return base, true
	case *ast.IndexExpr:
		// Generic like Set[T] or Set[string]? Receiver is like Set[T] (with type param, not concrete)
		return baseTypeName(t.X)
	case *ast.IndexListExpr:
		return baseTypeName(t.X)
	case *ast.SelectorExpr:
		// e.g., bytes.Buffer? Unlikely for receiver (must be local type), but handle
		return t.Sel.Name, false
	default:
		return "", false
	}
}

func matchesWithTitle(re *regexp.Regexp, recv, name string, isMethod bool) bool {
	if re.MatchString(name) {
		return true
	}
	if re.MatchString(goTitle(name)) {
		return true
	}
	if isMethod {
		combined := goTitle(recv) + name
		if re.MatchString(combined) {
			return true
		}
		if re.MatchString(goTitle(combined)) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func containsQualifier(typeStr, qual string) bool {
	// Check if typeStr contains "qual." as substring
	return strings.Contains(typeStr, qual+".")
}

func buildImportString(m map[string]string) string {
	if len(m) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	if len(m) == 1 {
		for path, alias := range m {
			if alias == "" {
				return "import \"" + path + "\""
			} else if alias == "." || alias == "_" {
				return "import " + alias + " \"" + path + "\""
			} else {
				return "import " + alias + " \"" + path + "\""
			}
		}
	}
	// Multiple: group std vs external?
	var stdLines []string
	var extLines []string
	for path, alias := range m {
		var line string
		if alias == "" {
			line = "\"" + path + "\""
		} else if alias == "." || alias == "_" {
			line = alias + " \"" + path + "\""
		} else {
			line = alias + " \"" + path + "\""
		}
		if strings.Contains(path, ".") {
			extLines = append(extLines, line)
		} else {
			stdLines = append(stdLines, line)
		}
	}
	// Sort each group
	sortStrs(stdLines)
	sortStrs(extLines)
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString("import (\n")
	for _, l := range stdLines {
		sb.WriteString("\t" + l + "\n")
	}
	if len(stdLines) > 0 && len(extLines) > 0 {
		sb.WriteString("\n")
	}
	for _, l := range extLines {
		sb.WriteString("\t" + l + "\n")
	}
	sb.WriteString(")")
	return sb.String()
}

func sortStrs(s []string) {
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		for j := i + 1; j < len(s); j++ {
			if s[j] < s[i] {
				s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
			}
		}
	}

For struct direct with no fields (T struct{}), body creates tr := T{} (ignoring tt.tr). For generic direct (Set etc.), creates s := &Set[string]{} (ignoring tt.s).

func extractFuncs(srcFile *ast.File, otherFiles map[string]*ast.File, fset *token.FileSet, isTestFile bool, onlyRe, exclRe *regexp.Regexp, exportedOnly bool) []FuncInfo {
	var out []FuncInfo
	for _, decl := range srcFile.Decls {
		fd, ok := decl.(*ast.FuncDecl)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		name := fd.Name.Name
		// Skip Test* in test files
		if isTestFile && strings.HasPrefix(name, "Test") {
			continue
		}
		isMethod := fd.Recv != nil && len(fd.Recv.List) > 0
		var recvName string
		var recvTypeAST ast.Expr
		var recvTypeBase string
		var recvIsPtr bool
		if isMethod {
			rf := fd.Recv.List[0]
			if len(rf.Names) > 0 {
				recvName = rf.Names[0].Name
			}
			recvTypeAST = rf.Type
			recvTypeBase, recvIsPtr = baseTypeName(rf.Type)
		}
		// Filtering
		if exportedOnly {
			if !isExported(name) {
				continue
			}
		}
		if onlyRe != nil {
			if !matchesWithTitle(onlyRe, recvTypeBase, name, isMethod) {
				continue
			}
		}
		if exclRe != nil {
			if matchesWithTitle(exclRe, recvTypeBase, name, isMethod) {
				continue
			}
		}
		// Build FuncInfo (params, results, etc. will be filled later)
		fi := FuncInfo{
			Name: name,
			IsMethod: isMethod,
			RecvName: recvName,
			RecvType: recvTypeBase,
			RecvTypeAST: recvTypeAST,
			RecvIsPointer: recvIsPtr,
			Decl: fd,
		}
		if isMethod {
			fi.TestName = testNameForMethod(recvTypeBase, name)
		} else {
			fi.TestName = testNameForFunc(name)
		}
		out = append(out, fi)
	}
	return out
}

func baseTypeName(expr ast.Expr) (string, bool) {
	// Returns base type name and isPointer
	switch t := expr.(type) {
	case *ast.Ident:
		return t.Name, false
	case *ast.StarExpr:
		base, _ := baseTypeName(t.X)
		return base, true
	case *ast.IndexExpr:
		// Generic like Set[T] or Set[string]? Receiver is like Set[T] (with type param, not concrete)
		return baseTypeName(t.X)
	case *ast.IndexListExpr:
		return baseTypeName(t.X)
	case *ast.SelectorExpr:
		// e.g., bytes.Buffer? Unlikely for receiver (must be local type), but handle
		return t.Sel.Name, false
	default:
		return "", false
	}
}

func matchesWithTitle(re *regexp.Regexp, recv, name string, isMethod bool) bool {
	if re.MatchString(name) {
		return true
	}
	if re.MatchString(goTitle(name)) {
		return true
	}
	if isMethod {
		combined := goTitle(recv) + name
		if re.MatchString(combined) {
			return true
		}
		if re.MatchString(goTitle(combined)) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
